findings.section: entire draft (launch-surface table item 2; phase overview; trailing changelog)
findings.criterion: all — an unparseable plan cannot serve any criterion
findings.message: This register item is STILL UNRESOLVED, and worse, the changelog now falsely claims it fixed. The "Round-3 re-emission, deduplicated" emission contains: (a) launch-surface item 2 still broken mid-sentence — "envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)" — with an ENTIRE second copy of the document (North Star included) embedded inside the backtick span, then a dangling ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3)" stitch fragment; (b) the old double-numbered phase headers ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 —", and TWO headers titled "Phase 4") alive inside that embedded copy, plus a THIRD partial copy after the changelog begins; (c) raw unapplied search/replace markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) sitting in the text, including an unmerged edit that leaves BOTH "Seven phases" and "Eight phases, numbered 0–7" as competing overview sentences. The changelog's claim "Exactly ONE North Star copy remains" is verifiably false of this very emission — there are at least three. A plan whose own changelog misreports its content fails the honesty standard the plan preaches on every page. As a bored investor: three rounds have been spent on re-emission mechanics and the deliverable is still not a document a Foreman wave can be cut from. Not lockable.

findings.section: Phase 1 beacon consume-time rule × Phase 3 eager owner finalize
findings.criterion: 1 (finalize fires from both the owning orchestrator and reconcile-dead)
findings.message: The strengthened beacon rule defeats Stage-0 decision 4. To consume the CAS a finalizer must "(a) BE the beacon-minting process this boot (PID + boot-token match against its own in-memory token) and (b) still HOLD the live exclusive bind." An owning orchestrator is a child `claude` process — it is never the process holding the 8777 bind, so under this rule EVERY eager owner finalize is structurally forced to `finalize-deferred`, collapsing the locked BOTH-paths design to sweep-only capture with up-to-30-minute latency, and making decision 4's eager path dead code. The plan never says how an orchestrator's finalize is proxied into the beaconed process (an HTTP call to the service? an in-process hook on session-end?). Either specify the proxy mechanism explicitly, or admit the eager path is really "the beaconed service finalizing on the session-end event" and rewrite the writer table row 1 to say so. As written, the two strongest sections of the plan contradict each other.

findings.criterion: 3 (a later live finalize can still measure)
findings.message: The deferred→`unmeasured` terminality rule says "only the audited repair path may ever revisit it" — but the only repair path defined anywhere in the plan is hardcoded to an allowlist of exactly the 3 intake session ids and refuses a second run. The cited escape hatch is structurally unavailable for any record terminated by `DEFER_RETRY_MAX`. Concrete failure: a munging-function bug for one dirname class makes those sidecars look "absent" for 20 sweeps → records terminate at `unmeasured`; the bug is later fixed, the sidecars exist in the archive, and nothing can ever measure them — a software bug converted into permanent, unrepairable data loss, exactly the "burned latch" class criterion 3 exists to kill, just relocated from hermetic contexts to the sweep itself. Either define a general (still audited, still gated) re-open tool, or make exhaustion re-checkable when the correlation function version changes.

Bored-investor core complaint: the one measured record (2.76M tok / 445s in `general`) exists TODAY, and rendering it as a separate rollup line is a surfaces-only change with zero dependency on the CAS, beacon, parser fence, or choke-point launcher — yet the plan gates it behind Phases 1–4. The stated justification ("surfaces render real substrate output, not placeholders") is vacuous for data that is already real substrate output. Criterion 2 could produce a visible dashboard receipt in the FIRST wave, de-risking the entire surfaces/consumer-enumeration work early and giving John a number on screen weeks sooner. The wave-ordering foresight optimizes soak time for the riskiest primitive but never weighs time-to-first-visible-value; a plan this long with the first dashboard pixel at Phase 5 is a sequencing choice that should be defended or changed, not defaulted.

findings.section: Phase 3 unwrapped shared-cwd walk-through × Phase 5 honest counting
findings.message: Phase 3 mints synthetic child rows (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`, `parent_session_id: S`) for unwrapped sub-agents, and Phase 5 defines "N measured of M total" over registry sessions — but nothing specifies whether a child row is a "session" in either N or M. Both answers are wrong without a rule: counting them inflates M with entities that were never registry sessions (the exact inflation pathology criterion 6 targets, in a new costume); excluding them from N while summing their tokens makes token totals and session counts inconsistent on the same surface. The interaction is left for Stage 2 to improvise, in the one area the North Star explicitly says must be honest. Specify the counting rule for child records now.

findings.section: Phase 7 ship receipt / Phase 6 outcome expectations
findings.message: The final backfill receipt is "the coverage-report ratio moved" — an unfalsifiable gate. Moving from 0.9% to 1.8% "moved." The intake evidence gives the plan a quantified expectation it declines to use: ~55 sidecar dirs carry the deterministic marker against a 109-session target population, so the plan can and should state an expected-recovered band (e.g. "recovered ≈ the marker-bearing population; a shortfall >20% below the Phase-0 manifest count is an investigation trigger, not a shrug"). Without a numeric expectation, a backfill run that silently recovers 6 sessions because of a correlation bug still passes Phase 7. Honest labeling of outcomes is necessary but not sufficient — the ship gate must compare the outcome against what the intake evidence says should have been recoverable.

"After a long outage the first boot sweep catches up before engine pruning windows matter" is asserted with zero evidence about the engine's actual retention/pruning window — the very class of unverified assumption the plan forbids elsewhere. If the service is down (or the machine off) longer than the engine's pruning horizon, forward orphan sidecars are deleted before any sweep sees them, and those sessions become permanently invisible with no honest record (they never got a deferred stamp because they were never registered). Either cite the observed pruning behavior, or have the boot sweep mint honest `unmeasured` markers for registry sessions whose sidecars are gone, so the loss is visible rather than silent.

Phase 3 bundles the choke-point helper, five spawner-family wirings (including modifying the agy-dispatch skill outside this repo), observed-id readback, the zombie-hunter decouple (the plan's own named safety-critical adjacency), the widened sweep with terminality, the per-file orphan correlator, AND an interim production deploy — easily three waves of work under one header, with the safety-critical change buried mid-list. Every other phase is single-purpose. Concentrating the highest safety-adjacency risk and a live deploy in the same over-stuffed wave maximizes the chance the zombie-coverage gate gets run against a moving target. Split the zombie-decouple + its required gate into its own wave boundary.
